title: SecOps-NG Metric (KPI / KRI)
description: A metric entry in the SecOps-NG metrics catalog. Each entry defines a single KPI (key performance indicator) or KRI (key risk indicator) that can be computed deterministically from the lower layers of the content model — playbook step transitions, detection firings, telemetry events, and/or control attestations. SecOps-NG does NOT define a new metrics standard; the catalog is a thin overlay that names common operator metrics (MTTD, MTTR, coverage, control-effectiveness) and binds each one to the content artifacts it measures via the shared `stable_id` shape used by the playbook / detection / control / telemetry layers.

stable_id.description: SecOps-NG stable identifier for this metric. Namespace convention: `kpi.<slug>@v<semver>` for KPIs, `kri.<slug>@v<semver>` for KRIs. Same lexical shape as every other layer of the content model so any layer can cross-reference any other without translation.

content_version.description: Semantic version of this metric content artifact.

kind.description: KPI = performance indicator (how well operations are running). KRI = risk indicator (how much residual exposure remains). The namespace prefix MUST agree with this field.

summary.description: One-paragraph operator-facing description of what this metric expresses and why it matters.

unit.description: Unit of measure. Use the smallest natural unit (seconds, count) and let the consumer rescale for display. `ratio` is dimensionless 0..1; `percent` is 0..100; `count` is a non-negative integer.

direction.description: Whether lower values or higher values represent a better outcome. Required so dashboards can colour deltas consistently.

target.description: Optional operator target for this metric. Compilers may emit this to a dashboard threshold or an alert rule.

thresholds.description: Optional banded thresholds (e.g. warn / breach). Evaluated in order; the first matching band wins.

measurement.description: How a consumer computes the value of this metric. The catalog entry is the contract — the actual computation lives in the compile target.

source.description: Where the inputs come from. `workflow` = playbook step transitions (durations, completions). `telemetry` = OCSF event stream. `detection` = detection firings / suppressions. `control` = control attestation state. `composite` = combination, see `inputs`.

aggregation.description: How individual observations roll up to a single metric value over the evaluation window.

formula.description: Human-readable formula in plain text. Free-form so authors can describe nuance (e.g. 'exclude duplicate alerts merged within 5 minutes'). The compile target is the source of truth for executable form.

inputs.description: Named inputs the formula consumes. Each input MAY bind to a stable_id elsewhere in the content model (telemetry class, detection rule, control, playbook step). The shape is documentation; the linter checks target existence.

field.description: Dot-path into the bound artifact (e.g. an OCSF field path) when applicable.

window.description: Evaluation window. Duration is ISO-8601 (e.g. P30D, PT24H). `sliding` = window slides per evaluation; otherwise the window is tumbling.

playbook_refs.description: Stable IDs of playbooks this metric is associated with. Each entry MAY pin a specific CACAO step.

external_refs.description: Pointers to upstream regulatory or framework references that motivate this metric (NIS2 Articles, ENISA guidance, ISO 27004, CIS measures). Plain text + URL only; no internal infra references per forward-public hygiene.

maintainer.description: Working-group mailbox or community handle. Generic role addresses only; no individual lead names per directive #7.

allOf.description: stable_id namespace prefix MUST agree with kind: kpi.* for kpi, kri.* for kri.
